Verdict: ACCEPTThe new note’s mathematical conclusions are sound under the foundational freezing results it explicitly invokes. The partial-connector degree argument, boundary inventory, omitted-path and cycle accounting, uniform constructions, mixed inventory, and conditional coefficient-one corollary all check out.There is one definite, nonblocking coordinate error in §4: the smallest occupied column is 2, not 1. Correcting it preserves the blank boundary columns, receiver closure, all inventories, and both obstruction claims.My acceptance concerns the written mathematics. I have not executed the Python or Lean files, inspected execution receipts, or used reported finite checks or previous review verdicts as proof. The standard-elbow freezing theorem and even-bridge completion theorem remain explicitly identified foundational dependencies.1. Exact correction in §4The supplied neutral-pair coordinates have greatest occupied original row  $H+5$ , attained by the selected support
$$(H+5,W+4).$$
The additional neutral-pair support at row  $9$  does not exceed this because  $H\ge4$ .After
$$(r,c)\longmapsto(c,r+1),$$
the largest occupied column of  $C(W,H)$  is therefore  $H+6$ . The left image consequently has minimum occupied column
$$H+8-(H+6)=2.$$
The right image has maximum occupied column
$$(H+6)+(H+2)=2H+8.$$
A precise replacement for the sentence in §4 is:All occupied columns lie between  $2$  and  $2H+8$ , inclusive. Thus both end columns of the  $(W+12)$ -by- $(2H+12)$  board are blank.The stated upper bound  $2H+9$  was valid but loose.There is also a small wording clarification available: “images of this ENTIRE block” should mean images of the entire occupied configuration, followed by blank padding. Reflecting the entire ambient rectangle would send its blank column  $H+9$  to column  $-1$ . Every occupied vertex lies inside the new board, so the construction itself is well defined.2. The partial-connector degree and boundary proof is correctEach interval has at most two incidencesThe proof in §§1–2 correctly identifies interval sides as the objects that control connector degree.Feasibility forces both neighboring columns of a TT column to be BB: each selected corner of the TT column already has its paired selected corner as its one occupied neighbor. Neither horizontal neighbor can therefore be occupied. Because the end columns are not TT, the BB–TT components are precisely odd alternating intervals
$$\mathrm{BB},\mathrm{TT},\ldots,\mathrm{BB}.$$
Each contributes one to  $\#\mathrm{BB}-\#\mathrm{TT}$ , establishing that their number is  $L$ .A BB port beside a TP column is necessarily an end of its interval. For a fixed side of a fixed interval, there is only one potentially adjacent TP column. That column has one endpoint, and that endpoint belongs to one actual PP terminal path. Since a selected path creates one connector and chooses one port at each terminal, that interval side supplies at most one incidence.This also handles the potentially troublesome cases:A singleton BB interval has two distinct sides, even though they belong to the same column.A connector loop must use both sides. The two terminals of a TP–TP path are distinct degree-one vertices of the PP multigraph, so they cannot both obtain their incidence from the same adjacent TP column.Parallel connectors retain separate edge identities and consume their incidences separately.Thus the connector multigraph has degree at most two, counting a loop twice. No freezing, orientation, monotonicity, or port-coverage hypothesis has entered this proof.The boundary marks are distinct and have degree at most oneMarks in different bands are automatically different interval vertices.Within an even-width band, an interval containing both end columns would have even length, contradicting the odd length of a BB–TT–…–BB interval. Hence a first-column mark and a final-column mark cannot coincide. This proves
$$B=k+t$$
as an actual count of distinct marked vertices.Each marked interval loses at least one possible connector incidence because one of its ends is on the packet boundary. Its degree is therefore at most one. For odd width, a first-marked interval may contain both boundary columns; it then has degree zero and still carries just one mark under the stated convention.Consequently:no marked vertex lies on a cycle;a nontrivial path has at most two marks, at its endpoints;an isolated vertex has at most one mark.The multigraph classification in §2 is valid with the stated conventions for loops and parallel edges. It gives exactly
$$L-a=h_0+h_1+h_2,\qquad B=h_1+2h_2.$$
There is no missing exceptional case here.3. The exact cycle and omitted-path accounting is correctThe supplied PP ledger follows directly from the column weights:
$$S=L+\frac{\#\mathrm{BP}-\#\mathrm{TP}}2.$$
For a matching-closed packet,
$$\#\mathrm{TP}=2\alpha+\gamma,\qquad
\#\mathrm{BP}=2\beta+\gamma,$$
so
$$S=L+\beta-\alpha.$$
Using  $\alpha=a+u$  and the connector inventory gives
$$\begin{aligned}
S
&=(L-a)+\beta-u\\
&=h_0+h_1+h_2+\beta-u,
\end{aligned}$$
and hence
$$\boxed{S-B=h_0+\beta-h_2-u.}$$
This proves the claimed equivalence for every permitted partial selection:
$$\boxed{S\ge B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad h_2+u\le h_0+\beta.}$$
The contributions can be read as follows:ObjectContribution after subtracting the boundary budgetUnmarked connector path component $+1$ Once-marked connector path component $0$ Twice-marked connector path component $-1$ Connector cycle $0$ Actual BP–BP matching path $+1$ Omitted TP–TP matching path $-1$ Omission is accounted for exactlyThe definition of  $u$  correctly includes both forced omissions and deliberate omissions of attachable paths. Every omitted TP–TP path retains its unit debit in the PP ledger; it contributes no connector edge.There is no need for a separate correction according to why the path was omitted.For example, removing one selected edge from an unmarked connector cycle produces an unmarked connector path component. The increase of one in  $h_0$  is exactly canceled by the increase of one in  $u$ . The reserve does not change merely because a connector was omitted.The cycle correction is present exactly onceA connector cycle has equal numbers of interval vertices and connector edges, so it contributes zero to  $L-a$ . Therefore  $h_0$ , which counts only unmarked path components, needs no additional cycle debit.If instead
$$i_0=h_0+c$$
counts all unmarked components, then
$$S-B=i_0+\beta-h_2-u-c$$
is correct. Subtracting  $c$  from the formula already expressed using  $h_0$  would undercount.The two-parallel-edge example correctly distinguishes the connector cycle from the PP cycles and correctly assigns it zero contribution.The injection interpretation has the stated scopeThe finite-set interpretation is sound:resources are unmarked connector path components and actual BP–BP paths;demands are twice-marked connector path components and omitted TP–TP paths.The cardinality inequality is equivalent to the existence of an abstract injection. It does not establish a local or geometrically constrained injection. The note accurately preserves that distinction and leaves the required universal geometric allocation theorem open.4. The coefficient-one corollary does not reuse resourcesThe supplied receiver-overlap correction is valid and essential.If two distinct global endpoint components meet the same physical tile, their endpoints must occupy opposite corners. The remaining corners cannot be endpoints, since either would connect the components, and cannot be selected, since either would see two occupied neighbors. Thus the tile has exactly two diagonal endpoints and no selections.Such a shared tile contributes exactly two to the difference between the receiver-union charge and the sum of individual component charges. This proves the correction
$$\rho_{\rm union}=\sum_K\rho_K+2N.$$
Under disjoint physical packets and complete receiver closure, the physical tiles partition into:packet tiles;outside endpoint-free tiles;the outside receiver union.Consequently the exact global identity is
$$\mathrm{margin}
=\sum_J S_J+D_{\rm out}-q+R_{\rm out}-2N_{\rm out}.$$
Substituting the local identity gives equation (5):
$$\mathrm{margin}
=\sum_J\bigl[B_J+h_{0,J}+\beta_J-h_{2,J}-u_J\bigr]
+D_{\rm out}-q+R_{\rm out}-2N_{\rm out}.$$
The resource ownership is correct at each stage:Every BB/TT column contributes to one interval.Connector components partition those interval vertices and the selected connector edges.Each selected connector represents a distinct actual TP–TP path.BP–BP paths are different PP components and supply no connector edges.Omitted TP–TP paths supply no resource credit.Packet surplus is included directly as  $S_J$ .Internal receiver overlaps are already included in  $S_J$ . $N_{\rm out}$  counts only outside shared tiles.An internal allocation satisfying
$$h_{2,J}+u_J\le h_{0,J}+\beta_J$$
therefore leaves
$$S_J\ge B_J.$$
The further condition
$$q+2N_{\rm out}\le\sum_J B_J$$
then implies the half-area bound, using  $D_{\rm out},R_{\rm out}\ge0$ . The version using the actual unused  $D_{\rm out}+R_{\rm out}$  is also valid.One precision matters when describing this ownership: different internal resource objects need not occupy disjoint whole physical tiles. An interval column and a terminal column can occupy different halves of one tile. Their additivity comes from distinct column contributions in the exact PP ledger. Physical-tile disjointness is required between packets and the outside classes; it is not an additional claim about every individual internal reserve object.Thus the coefficient-one statement is a correct conditional sufficient corollary. It does not supply the missing internal allocation or outside budget inequality.5. The uniform frozen two-edge cycle construction checks outThe base PP inventory follows from the displayed matchingAfter the collision transformation, the original upper elbow bar becomes the sole TP–TP path in column  $5$ . It runs between bands
$$2\quad\text{and}\quad W/2+2$$
and uses  $W/2$  matching edges.The remaining matching edges decompose as follows: $W/2-1$  lower-bar edges become PP loops;the two right-leg columns contribute  $H/2$  and  $H/2-1$  TP–BP edges;the short tip and the neutral pair contribute one TP–BP edge each.Thus
$$\alpha=1,\quad \beta=0,\quad \gamma=H+1,\quad
\#\text{PP loops}=W/2-1,$$
and these account for
$$W/2+(W/2-1)+(H+1)=W+H$$
actual matching edges.At each TP–TP terminal, column  $4$  is BB and column  $6$  is BP. The added TT column  $3$  creates the exact interval
$$\mathrm{BB}2-\mathrm{TT}3-\mathrm{BB}4.$$
The port assertions therefore hold uniformly, including at the smallest allowed parameters.The two images create precisely the asserted connector cycleIn the union construction:the four added selections coincide at column  $H+5$ ;all other occupied vertices of the left image have column at most  $H+3$ ;all other occupied vertices of the right image have column at least  $H+7$ .The common TT pairs are separated from both occupied cores by blank columns. They retain only their paired selected neighbor, and no new occupied adjacency appears.The two TP–TP paths lie at columns  $H+3$  and  $H+7$ . Their unique ports lie at columns  $H+4$  and  $H+6$ , respectively, and belong to the same interval
$$\mathrm{BB}(H+4)-\mathrm{TT}(H+5)-\mathrm{BB}(H+6)$$
in each of the two terminal bands.Those two bands are distinct. The connector graph therefore has two distinct vertices joined by two parallel edges. Both ports are forced, so the cycle cannot be removed by selecting alternative ports while retaining both paths.Feasibility, uniqueness and freezing persistThe endpoint cores remain disjoint and acquire no new endpoint adjacency. Their perfect-matching problems therefore factor, preserving uniqueness.For freezing, the construction can be viewed as two separated frozen neutral cores with the common TT pairs added feasibly. Every original or retained witness remains present. The four shared selections are actual vertices included once; their identification removes no endpoint support because they are separated from the cores.This is a valid inheritance argument relative to the neutral-pair freezing supplier.The reflection does change the source’s physical column phase. That causes no accounting problem here: the new packet is the whole new even-by-even board, and its surplus is recomputed from its actual area and counts. No source receiver credit is transported or added to the new surplus.All counts agreeThe half-area of the common board is
$$(W+12)(H+6).$$
Therefore
$$\begin{aligned}
|T|&=2(H+11)-4=2H+18,\\
|M|&=2(W+H),\\
S&=(W+12)(H+6)-(2H+18)-2(W+H)\\
 &=WH+4W+8H+54.
\end{aligned}$$
The PP inventories add across the endpoint cores:
$$\alpha=2,\quad \beta=0,\quad \gamma=2(H+1),\quad
\#\text{PP loops}=W-2.$$
Hence  $L=S+2$ .The full board has
$$B=2\frac{W+12}{2}=W+12.$$
The two cycle vertices are unmarked. Every other connector vertex is isolated, so
$$c=1,\quad u=h_2=0,\quad h_1=B,\quad h_0=S-B.$$
All displayed cycle-family formulas follow.6. The uniform missing-port construction also checks outThe two new original selections
$$(3,5),\qquad(3,W+4)$$
are distinct and nonadjacent for every allowed  $W$ . Each sees exactly its endpoint immediately below; the other three neighboring positions are blank. The old selected vertices gain no occupied neighbor.The endpoint set and matching are unchanged, preserving uniqueness.The freezing argument correctly starts from the original neutral configuration, before the four TT additions. It adds two feasible selections and retains every old witness. The equivalent description involving removal of the four TT additions from  $C(W,H)$  is a coordinate recipe; freezing follows from the original neutral base.After transformation, the two terminal endpoint rows are  $5$  and  $W+4$ . At each terminal:the left neighboring column is BT;the right neighboring column is BP.Thus neither terminal has a BB port. The two selected supports at each terminal do not change that column-type obstruction.After the left shift and embedding,
$$|T|=H+9,\qquad |M|=W+H,$$
and
$$\begin{aligned}
S
&=(W+12)(H+6)-(H+9)-(W+H)\\
&=WH+5W+10H+63.
\end{aligned}$$
The PP inventory remains
$$\alpha=1,\quad\beta=0,\quad\gamma=H+1,\quad
\#\text{PP loops}=W/2-1.$$
There are no connector edges, so
$$a=0,\quad u=1,\quad L=S+1.$$
All intervals are isolated, giving
$$c=h_2=0,\qquad h_1=B,\qquad h_0=L-B.$$
Accordingly,
$$S-B=h_0-1.$$
The residual debit is exactly one, and omitting  $u$  would overstate the reserve by one.7. The mixed inventory and obstruction claims are correctFor the shifted collision block, the interval
$$\mathrm{BB}0-\mathrm{TT}1-\mathrm{BB}2$$
contains the first-boundary mark in each terminal band. Its one connector joins two marked vertices, so
$$h_2=1,\qquad c=u=0.$$
Its surplus is
$$S=WH+5W+10H+61.$$
Writing  $B_0=W+12$ , the three block types have:Block type $c$  $h_2$  $u$  $h_0$ Cycle $1$  $0$  $0$  $S-B_0$ Boundary collision $0$  $1$  $0$  $S-B_0+1$ Missing port $0$  $0$  $1$  $S-B_0+1$ Stacking preserves the ordinary row phase because  $W+12$  is even. Occupied rows in each block lie in  $4,\ldots,W+5$ , leaving a blank separation between successive blocks. Hence matching components, PP paths and connectors cannot cross between blocks.It follows that
$$c=r_C,\qquad h_2=r_B,\qquad u=r_U,\qquad \beta=0,$$
and
$$B=(r_C+r_B+r_U)(W+12).$$
The surplus is the stated sum of block surpluses, and
$$\boxed{h_0=S-B+r_B+r_U.}$$
An additional consistency check is
$$h_1=B-2r_B,$$
which gives  $B=h_1+2h_2$  exactly.The three effects therefore coexist independently on actual frozen configurations.Their interpretation is also correctly restricted:the cycle family obstructs universal connector acyclicity;the missing-port family obstructs universal port coverage;the collision family obstructs an unconditional injection of boundary marks into distinct connector components.The excesses over the packet target are respectively
$$\begin{aligned}
S_C-B_0&=WH+3W+8H+42,\\
S_B-B_0&=WH+4W+10H+49,\\
S_U-B_0&=WH+4W+10H+51.
\end{aligned}$$
All are positive throughout the parameter range. Every nonempty mixed stack likewise has positive excess. These are rule obstructions, and the note does not claim that they disprove the target inequality.8. Dependency and formal-verification limitsThe supplied neutral-pair argument is consistent with the new uses. Its only inter-piece endpoint contact is the bridge  $p-q$ , separating two even endpoint sets. Such a bridge cannot occur in a perfect matching. The completed pieces and restored supports are the ones stated, and the new constructions preserve the relevant selected and retained witnesses.The full standard-elbow freezing proof and the general even-bridge composition theorem are cited suppliers whose complete statements and proofs are not reproduced here. Acceptance is relative to those mathematical suppliers. Their previous review labels do not replace them.The pasted Lean source has the restricted scope described in §7:Piece encodes the path/cycle decomposition and mark bounds.The list lemmas establish inventory arithmetic for that representation.The compensation theorem assumes the PP ledger and selected/omitted-path inventory.The global theorem assumes the global ledger and ownership budgets.The family-margin lemmas assume the family inventory formulas.It does not independently construct the grid-to-graph adapter, establish port ownership, prove the coordinate constructions, or construct the missing geometric injection. The manuscript already discloses these boundaries correctly.Likewise, the pasted checker visibly tracks parallel edges, loop incidences, interval sides and omitted paths in a manner consistent with the written argument. Its imported validation functions and execution results are separate evidence. This review certifies none of those reported execution outcomes.
